notes: Detection is correct, but the reverse-proxy-specific placeholder list lives in the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher (a layering smell); tests are excellent and include unit, handler and integration repros.
Works and is well tested, but it hardcodes reverse_proxy placeholder names inside the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher, which is a layering smell compared with exposing generic placeholder names.
Clean AST walk with member-call exclusion, dedup and a cloned API, classifier kept in reverseproxy; tests include unit, handler, ph() retry and a Caddyfile integration repro of the issue.

Correct generic `Placeholders()` API with dedup and a dynamic flag; tests are strong (integration, unit, request-only table, direct `ph()` retry), though the dedup and target checks add slight extra complexity.

Production code is essentially identical to the reference plus a doc update; tests cover the ph() variant via the parametrized existing test, several request-only expressions and a comprehension-based dynamic name, but do not check body preservation.
Implementation matches the reference exactly, and tests cover request-only, escaped, lookalike, upstream.host and `ph()` cases plus a `ph()` variant of the status-code retry test.
Correct and very well tested, but it embeds reverse-proxy knowledge (including rp. shorthand normalization) in caddyhttp and adds a speculative value-type case.

Functionally correct with thorough tests, but it puts reverse-proxy knowledge (plus a needless `rp.` mapping) in caddyhttp and relies on an early-return guard to make an overwrite-style assignment safe.

Walks the checked AST, reports whether all placeholder names are known, and keeps the response-placeholder list in reverseproxy; the extra rp.* names are harmless, and the tests are thorough, including an end-to-end test where a dynamic placeholder name actually resolves to status_code.
Correct fix with extensive tests including an end-to-end dynamic-name retry, but it adds unnecessary raw `rp.*` aliases that are never runtime placeholders and a duplicate string-literal helper.

Correct names-plus-complete API and classifier in reverseproxy; minor oddities are the struct copy in the type switch and relying on AsLiteral returning nil; detection and body-echo regression tests are good.
Sound AST-based detection reusing `isCELCaddyPlaceholderCall`, with very thorough tests; the defensive value-type `MatchExpression` branch is unnecessary but harmless.
Correct AST-based placeholder collection with a dynamic flag and a well-placed classifier in reverseproxy; end-to-end tests cover request-only cases, a direct ph() call, a dynamic name and latency.

Clean `Placeholders()` plus dynamic flag with logic kept in reverseproxy; good tests covering request-only cases, direct `ph()`, dynamic names and latency, with only minor nits (no slice clone, mutating helper method).
Works, but it reinvents ast.NewExprVisitor with a custom visitor type, places reverse-proxy placeholder knowledge in caddyhttp, and slightly muddles the RetryMatchRaw doc.
Correct, but it embeds reverse-proxy placeholder names in caddyhttp, reimplements `ast.NewExprVisitor` with a custom type, and slightly degrades the `retry_match` doc.

Clean use of ast.MatchDescendants/FunctionMatcher with a names-plus-dynamic API, though Placeholders() returns the internal slice without cloning; detection tests are solid with one end-to-end regression test.

Walks the checked AST for `ph` calls and flags non-literal names as dynamic, keeping the response-placeholder list in reverseproxy; minor nit: `Placeholders()` returns the internal slice without cloning.

Elegant predicate API (ReferencesPlaceholder) that folds dynamic names in and keeps the classifier in reverseproxy; it has a broad detection table and a single end-to-end test but no CEL-level unit test.
Clean `ReferencesPlaceholder(func)` API that folds dynamic names in conservatively; a broad matcher-set table test and a POST body handler test, but no direct celmatcher unit test.
